The positive straight leg raise (SLR) at 9° is an exceptionally early and provocative sign, indicating significant nerve root irritation — typically seen in acute disc herniation with mechanical compression or inflammatory compromise of the L5 or S1 root. The absence of bowel/bladder dysfunction rules out cauda equina syndrome. Normal Achilles and patellar reflexes argue against *isolated* S1 or L4 root compromise (though S1 reflex can be spared early or in partial lesions), but do not exclude L5 radiculopathy — the L5 root does not contribute to a deep tendon reflex; its motor and sensory manifestations dominate. MRI is appropriately ordered to confirm location and severity.
